item.content:encoded:

🎙
🇷🇺
Statement by Permanent Representative of the Russian Federation to the International Organizations in Vienna
Mikhail Ulyanov
at the Seventh Session of the UN Conference on the Establishment of the Middle East Zone Free of Nuclear Weapons and Other Weapons of Mass Destruction
📍
New York, 16 November 2026
💬
We are compelled to note that, since our
last meeting
, the international security and nuclear non-proliferation landscape
has not undergone any significant improvement
.
The escalation in the Middle East has not subsided. Following the
unlawful and unprovoked
US-Israeli aggression
against Iran’s nuclear facilities,
which were under IAEA safeguards
, in June 2025, the United States and Israel embarked on a new and unprecedented escalation in February-April this year.
The war is still ongoing and has affected a number of other countries in the region. Unfortunately, despite the efforts being made, a sustainable peaceful settlement has yet to be achieved.
👉
The threat of a resumption of armed hostilities remains.
<…>
❌
The difficult situation prevailing today in the field of nuclear non-proliferation was also reflected in the fact that the Eleventh Review Conference of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), held here in New York this spring, concluded
without the adoption of a final document.
***
Now, more than ever, there is a pressing need for collective political and diplomatic efforts
aimed at de-escalating tensions and maintaining dialogue
across the entire range of issues related to regional security.
📄
A
sufficient number of relevant initiatives
are already on the table, covering either the entire Middle East or individual parts of the region. One such initiative is Russia’s
Concept of Collective Security in the Persian Gulf Region
, which was most recently updated in 2026.
***
For seven years now, the UN Conference on the Establishment of a Middle East Zone Free of Nuclear Weapons and Other Weapons of Mass Destruction has been building on the
substantial results
achieved in its earlier work.
In addition to the aforementioned consensus rule, we have a substantive political declaration; representatives of the IAEA and the OPCW Secretariats regularly participate in the forum’s proceedings; meetings of the intersessional Working Committee are held, and, more recently, have also been hosted by countries of the region; and the fifth session of the Conference, in 2024, was held in a review format for the first time.
☝️
All this provides a
solid foundation for further progress
.

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answer to a question
from
RT France
regarding media reports on the presence of French military personnel in Ukraine
(November 17, 2026)
❓
Question:
RFI has published an article
on the direct involvement of French military personnel in technical support and training activities in Ukraine. It notes that their deployment bypassed the law and parliament. What measures does the Russian MFA intend to take in light of these revelations?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
RFI’s report
on the presence of French military personnel in Ukraine as part of
“Operation Volya”
came as neither a surprise nor a revelation to us
.
Paris’s direct involvement in the Ukraine conflict has long been an open secret.
We have repeatedly pointed to the presence of Western military experts, instructors and mercenaries in Ukraine, including from France.
In October 2025,
Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service also reported
on French plans to deploy
a military contingent
to Ukraine. President
Emmanuel Macron
himself has repeatedly spoken of the possibility, or even the necessity, of such a move.
As is known,
large-scale
Coalition 2.0
exercises
are currently taking place in Poland to prepare for the deployment of multinational forces to Ukraine under the
“coalition of the willing”
, with French personnel forming their core.
This confirms that Paris and the other coalition capitals are quite serious about their intentions.
Given the scale of the assistance Paris provides to the AFU, including deliveries of technologically sophisticated weapons and the establishment of production facilities in Ukraine,
it would be naive to assume that French military specialists are not involved on the ground
.
☝️
We have no doubt that the extent of France’s direct or indirect involvement in hostilities will eventually become public knowledge.
If
RFI’s report
that the French parliament was not informed of military personnel taking part in an overseas operation is accurate, this would be
further evidence of the French authorities’ disregard for the views of their own citizens
.
Far from everyone in France supports the current leadership’s militarist course.
Many understand that it
does nothing to strengthen national security
and
creates unprecedented risks
of a direct confrontation with Russia. Indeed, French officials have long openly acknowledged that this is precisely what they are preparing for.
While France is reeling from
yet another wave of protests
, its authorities continue to act as though Ukraine were their overriding priority. Instead of addressing pressing social and economic problems,
Paris is becoming ever more deeply embroiled in the Ukraine conflict
, sparing no expense and seemingly prepared to risk the lives of its own military personnel.
As for measures on our part, these will be taken by
the Defence Ministry
and the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation
, rather than
the Foreign Ministry
.
As President
Vladimir Putin
has stated
,
foreign troops
, if deployed to Ukraine,
will become legitimate targets for the Russian military.
👉
We hope Paris understands this.

item.description: ⚡️ Russian Embassy in France’s response to a question from RIA Novosti on the presence of French military personnel in Ukraine (November 17, 2026) ❓ Question: According to media reports , French military personnel have been secretly deployed in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian soldiers and maintaining equipment. How does Russia assess these actions by France in support of the Kiev regime? ✍🏻 Answer: The information published by French media confirms what the French authorities have long tried to conceal and timidly denied. ❗️ By sending Ukraine not only weapons used to strike Russian cities and civilian facilities, but also its own military personnel, France has de facto become embroiled in the armed conflict on the side of the criminal Kiev regime . Russia has long and repeatedly warned that the presence of foreign contingents in Ukraine is unacceptable and that they would become legitimate targets for our Armed Forces . This marks another escalation by France , a NATO member, which undermines efforts to achieve a peaceful settlement of the Ukraine conflict and risks a direct clash between nuclear powers . 👉 Against this backdrop, France’s attempts to secure a seat at the negotiating table appear utterly cynical .

item.title: ⚡️ Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's statement on developments in the Middle East
item.description: ⚡️ Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's statement on developments in the Middle East (November 17, 2026) We note with regret another surge in tensions in the Persian Gulf , where the opposing sides have exchanged further strikes in recent days. Hits were recorded on Iran’s Qeshm Island and on the territory of Bahrain . Such attacks constitute a blatant violation of the sovereignty and security of states in the region and, to our deep regret, cause casualties and material damage. ❗️ Russia once again calls on all parties to the current confrontation , above all the US, which initiated it , to cease hostilities immediately. We consider attacks on civilians and any civilian facilities, including strikes on the territory of the Arab states of the Persian Gulf, utterly unacceptable . Russia consistently advocates resolving differences in this strategically important region at the negotiating table, taking into account the interests of every coastal state without exception. 🤝 W e stand ready to provide the necessary assistance towards this goal , including on the basis of the proposals set out in Russia’s Concept of Collective Security in the Persian Gulf Region , updated in May.

item.title: 🗓 On November 17, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov took part in the 21st East Asia Summit
item.description: 🗓 On November 17, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov took part in the 21st East Asia Summit ( #EAS ) in Manila . In his remarks , the Minister stressed the importance of strengthening the international legal foundations underpinning the work of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations ( #ASEAN ) and the region-wide mechanisms built around it. 👉 Sergey Lavrov's full remarks at the EAS Sergey Lavrov drew attention to the risks of undermining the ASEAN-centred system as Euro-Atlantic actors encroach on regional fora , violating ASEAN’s established rules and operating principles and introducing confrontational issues onto their agendas. The Minister also highlighted the militarisation of the region and the growing network of military blocs facilitating NATO’s expansion into Asia. Russia reaffirmed its consistent commitment to fostering a secure, conflict-free environment in the Asia-Pacific conducive to sustainable growth and cooperation on an equal footing. It also expressed its interest in maintaining an open, depoliticised dialogue within the EAS , with a focus on practical cooperation. Regional partners were briefed on Russia’s proposals for a seamless architecture of security and joint development across Eurasia , including by bringing together the capabilities of multilateral mechanisms such as the #SCO , #ASEAN and #EAEU , which pursue a broad, positive agenda . 👉 Sergey Lavrov's news conference following the EAS

🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov following
the 21st East Asia Summit
(Manila, November 17, 2026)
Key points
:
• I believe today's event was
useful
. It is mainly
European countries, Australia
and
Japan
that are politicising this forum.
•
An entire architecture has been built around
#ASEAN
–
the ASEAN Regional Forum
,
the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus
(ADMM-Plus), etc –
and everyone has always recognised ASEAN’s centrality within it
. Our Western colleagues are now trying
to undermine and dismantle
this inclusive, open and consensus-based architecture. They are trying to draw individual ASEAN countries into
exclusive military blocs
.
•
NATO members are actively expanding their presence in this region
, making little secret of their goal:
to contain the People’s Republic of China
. Everyone understands this. Beyond moving elements of NATO’s military infrastructure here, they have even devised a new concept: establishing
an Indo-Pacific Treaty Organisation
modelled on NATO.
•
Nothing good has ever come of NATO’s presence.
The Alliance’s
invasions of Iraq
,
the former Yugoslavia
and
Libya
, and its many other ventures, speak for themselves. Whenever NATO has operated beyond its members’ territory, these have been
military missions of a distinctly aggressive nature
. Nowhere has NATO’s armed intervention improved the situation. On the contrary,
it has left deep crises everywhere
, with neighbouring countries bearing the brunt of dealing with the consequences.
•
We sensed a desire among our ASEAN friends to uphold the founding principles
underpinning both the Association itself and its mechanisms for engagement with partners, including the East Asia Summits. If everyone treats the founders of this process –
the ASEAN countries
– with respect, all these meetings will be far more productive.
• Japanese PM
Sanae Takaichi
has already announced that she is
no longer satisfied
with the three non-nuclear principles
enshrined in
Japan’s Constitution
.
This will trigger a chain reaction
. There could be a domino effect. Many understand this, including ASEAN members. We will work with them
to prevent these adverse trends from materialising
.
🇷🇺
🇨🇳
🇺🇸
[
The trilateral meeting of the Leaders of Russia, China and the US
, scheduled for November 19 in Shenzhen],
is useful under any circumstances
, because these are three nuclear powers. Two of them are also the world’s largest economies. These countries have wide-ranging interests across the globe and interesting initiatives to offer.
Simply listening to one another is useful in itself
, particularly as no meeting in this format has ever been held before.
• As for
the agenda
of the meeting between
Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping
and
Donald Trump
, it has been agreed.
I will not comment
on what the other participants are saying about the substance of the forthcoming meeting.
That is not our practice
. It is broadly clear what the Leaders will discuss. They will have an opportunity for a free exchange of views. Be patient.
There is very little time left to wait.
• Why do the Europeans want a ceasefire in Ukraine? They want to deploy “stabilisation forces” immediately. They have been warned a thousand times: President
Vladimir Putin
, I and many other officials
have said
that
any deployment of “stabilisation forces” would mean Europe’s direct and unequivocal entry into the war.
• On the Ukraine crisis, I would like to reiterate what President
Vladimir Putin
recently emphasised
when commenting on the
“territorial issue”
: we are not fighting for territory,
we are fighting for people who have been deprived of the basic rights guaranteed by numerous documents.

🎙
Remarks
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at
the 21st East Asia Summit
(Manila, November 17, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
The Russia-ASEAN Summit held in Kazan
in June 2026 gave
a substantial boost
to deepening our strategic partnership
across the full range of areas set out in
the Plan of Action for 2026-2030
.
#ASEAN
’s foremost achievement is
the creation of a regional architecture
underpinned by clear legal agreements. Consistent adherence to these agreements has ensured the Association’s success as one of the key centres of the emerging
#MultipolarWorld
.
Today, stability in the Asia-Pacific region largely depends on whether we can preserve
the robust ecosystem of ASEAN-centred security and cooperation mechanisms
at a time when certain ASEAN partners are imposing
archaic bloc-based models
on the region –
“exclusive clubs”, “trios”
and
“quads”
.
❗️
Under the banner of indivisible security across the Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific regions,
NATO’s military capabilities are being actively drawn into this region.
Plans to establish
an Indo-Pacific Treaty Organisation
have been announced.
In July 2026, London unlawfully joined
the ASEAN Regional Forum
(
#ARF
), in breach of the principle of consensus that everyone had respected until then. In another violation of consensus rules,
Canada blocked Russia’s participation in an ARF event
, justifying its unlawful actions by saying that its NATO obligations took precedence.
👉
This shows utter disrespect for ASEAN and its central role in cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region.
***
We support the efforts of ASEAN and China to agree on a Code of Conduct in the South China Sea.
Attempts at external interference only make it harder to find solutions.
I must also address the Taiwan question.
Everyone seemingly declares their commitment to the one-China principle, yet many continue to insist on the need, and I quote,
“not to alter the status quo”
. In essence, this amounts to
an unacceptable attempt to push Taiwan towards independence
.
The main reason for the growing potential for conflict on the Korean Peninsula is
the pressure exerted on the DPRK through sanctions and military force
,
aggressive actions near its territory
, and
continuing military exercises and war games
, including those involving a nuclear component.
🚢
The issue of safe navigation is becoming global
, both because of
developments around the Arabian Peninsula
and because many Western countries have openly reverted to the piracy practised during colonial expansion
.
There are numerous other examples showing that
colonialism has not disappeared
, but merely taken on new forms.
In these circumstances, it is essential to secure equal opportunities for countries of the Global South
, help them build their own capabilities and ensure that they exercise effective control over their natural resources, retain the added value themselves and, of course, secure their rightful place in the global economy.
🌐
This requires strengthening
a space of equal and indivisible security
in keeping with ASEAN’s original goals, rather than creating new dividing lines.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On November 17, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Prime Minister of Laos
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇱🇦 On November 17, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Prime Minister of Laos Saleumxay Kommasith held a meeting on the sidelines of the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila. The Sides discussed priority tasks for strengthening the Russia-Laos strategic partnership , focusing on advancing bilateral political dialogue and practical cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, humanitarian affairs, the fuel and energy sector, and ICT. They also exchanged views on cooperation in multilateral fora , including the #EAS , the #SCO , #CICA and the #RussiaASEAN Dialogue Partnership. #RussiaLaos
